correctness.rationale: The support intervals for every subset are obtained from simplex summands; a greedy linear-functional argument proves they form a complete description. The exact reflection-containment criterion is applied to all leaf subsets and their complements. The singleton lower inequalities and full-leaf upper inequality give the claimed sharp lower bound for arbitrary non-symmetric centers, and force uniqueness at equality. Concavity of the count of intersecting hub simplices provides all remaining upper/lower inequalities at the proposed center. Exact-rational computations of 5,912 greedy orders through dimension six independently check finite instances; the proof holds for all k>=1.

originality.rationale: The natural simplex-sum stellohedron is established in arXiv:2109.09200. The inspected papers supply its realization and graph-distance properties but not the affine Minkowski-asymmetry factor or unique symmetry center. The explicit sharp ratio is not implied merely by a general finite LP formulation, and its uniqueness follows from new matching equality constraints. Searches for aliases and exact ratios identified no covering primary theorem. Earlier inradius results are distinct. Terminology and undiscovered equivalent sources remain risks; this is same-model review only.

value.rationale: The stellohedron is a canonical graph associahedron. The result fully classifies a natural affine-invariant extremal quantity and the unique optimizing point in each dimension, distinguishing it from previously studied Euclidean inradius and skeleton diameter. It supplies a dimension-dependent sharp closed form s=k/2+k/[2(2^k-1)], including nontrivial half-dimension growth and a hub/leaf center ratio approaching two. It is neither an arbitrary slice nor a known-table repetition.
